thread:
Maya: FYI initial bring-up for fenrir-8b (int6) finished in canary. Latency + mem look good but recall on longform QA drops ~4-6 pts vs baseline 13b-int8. Cost per 1k tokens ~22% lower.
Jorge: can you paste the eval numbers and config? which benchmarks? :thinking:
Maya: quick paste:
```
Benchmark: LongQA-500
Baseline (13b-int8): EM=72.4, F1=80.1, cost=$0.62/1k
Fenrir-8b-int6: EM=67.1, F1=74.8, cost=$0.48/1k
Delta: -5.3 EM, -5.3 F1, -22.6% cost
Latency p50: baseline 120ms -> fenrir 95ms
```
Liam: that's not trivial. what's slice-level breakdown? long contexts or multi-turn?
Maya: failure mostly >1200 tokens and long-hop trace questions. Short answers fine.
Anya: propose scorecard thresholds for GTN: set provisional routing rule: <=1k tokens -> fenrir-8b-int6; >1k tokens -> fallback to 13b-int8. Also enable 5% traffic shadow to 13b to catch drift. Add regression alert if F1 drop >3 pts on critical slices.
Jorge: what's unit econ impact for product? i.e., expected monthly cost delta if we flip 30% of traffic.
Maya: rough calc: current mix 100% 13b => baseline cost X. If 30% moves to fenrir, net cost down ~7% org-wide given token distribution skewed to short queries. I'll attach spreadsheet later.
GTM-Sam: product question: is quality loss visible to users? SLA ok? If fallback routing is implemented, can we guarantee no customer-visible regressions?
Anya: with routing by token-length and shadowing + rollback, customer-visible risk low. Recommend canary increment: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with metric gates on slice F1 and latency SLO.
Liam: also run priming sensitivity on top-5 failing prompts; sometimes priming reduces the gap.
Maya: agreed. Run priming sweep + small-context KV cache warmstart. Ops: need routing flag and rollout playbook.
Deploy-bot: canary deploy fenrir-8b-int6 -> env: canary-42 SUCCESS :sparkles:
Maya: Next steps: 1) Anya to draft routing flag config + scorecard gates, 2) Liam to run priming sweep on 500 failing examples, 3) Jorge to validate cost model and publish unit-econ note, 4) GTM-Sam to review product risk. Ping here when done.
Jorge: I'll get the unit econ note by EOD tomorrow.
Anya: I'll post the routing JSON and gate thresholds in #eng-platform when ready.
GTM-Sam: thanks all. Keep the summary short for the GTN playbook once we have numbers.
